recon_summary:
- **What it does:** CodeAF is an AI coding/agent platform that runs LLM-driven sessions, proposes and executes software tasks, plans/verifies changes, and supports TUI, CLI, headless, and remote multi-machine operation.
- **Tech stack:** Go-based system with internal packages (`session`, `exec`, `plan`, `factory`, `tui3`), LLM provider clients, MCP/connections, event journal/materialized views, relay/cluster consensus, and CI/Makefile workflows.
- **Untrusted input / attack surface:** User prompts and steering, model-generated tool calls/code, remote protocol/hosted sessions/pairing/device sync, MCP/connections/accounts, repository/PR content, and session/memory files.
- **Riskiest component:** The execution engine/tool belt (`internal/exec` plus task execution and permissions), because it can run code, modify files, and interact with external systems based on untrusted model or user input.

title: DVWA

report.verdict: 🔴 Not safe to ship: 9 critical issue(s) need fixing now.
report.plain_summary: Your website has nine serious weaknesses that could let a hacker take control of it. They could steal data, log in as anyone, or change accounts without permission. None of these have been fixed yet, so they should be treated as urgent.

items.title: OS Command Injection via Ping
items.plain: An attacker can trick the server into running any command they want, potentially stealing data or crashing the system.
items.fix: Use escapeshellarg($target) to safely escape the input: exec("ping -c 4 " . escapeshellarg($target), $output, $ret_var);

items.title: OS Command Injection via Shell Exec
items.plain: An attacker can execute arbitrary commands on the server by manipulating the input.
items.fix: Use escapeshellarg($target) to escape the input: $cmd = shell_exec('ping ' . escapeshellarg($target));

items.title: SQL Injection in Login Query
items.plain: An attacker can log in as any user or access sensitive data by entering special characters in the login form.
items.fix: Use prepared statements: $stmt = $pdo->prepare("SELECT * FROM users WHERE user = ? AND password = ?"); $stmt->execute([$user, $pass]);

items.title: SQL Injection in User ID Query
items.plain: An attacker can access or modify data belonging to other users by altering the user ID input.
items.fix: Use prepared statements: $stmt = $pdo->prepare("SELECT user_id FROM users WHERE user_id = ?"); $stmt->execute([$id]);

items.title: SQL Injection in Brute Force Query
items.plain: An attacker can bypass login restrictions or extract data from the database by manipulating the input.
items.fix: Use prepared statements: $stmt = $pdo->prepare("SELECT * FROM users WHERE user = ? AND password = ?"); $stmt->execute([$user, $pass]);

items.title: SQL Injection in Password Update
items.plain: An attacker can change passwords or access other users' data by manipulating the password input.
items.fix: Use prepared statements: $stmt = $pdo->prepare("UPDATE users SET password = ? WHERE user = ? LIMIT 1"); $stmt->execute([$pass_new, dvwaCurrentUser()]);

items.title: SQL Injection in CSRF Password Update
items.plain: An attacker can change passwords or access other users' data by manipulating the input.
items.fix: Use prepared statements: $stmt = $pdo->prepare("UPDATE users SET password = ? WHERE user = ?"); $stmt->execute([$pass_new, $current_user]);

items.title: SQL Injection in Credential Test
items.plain: An attacker can log in as any user or access sensitive data by entering special characters in the login form.
items.fix: Use prepared statements: $stmt = $pdo->prepare("SELECT * FROM users WHERE user = ? AND password = ?"); $stmt->execute([$user, $pass]);

items.title: Local File Inclusion via Variable
items.plain: An attacker can read or execute sensitive files on the server by manipulating the file path input.
items.fix: Validate and whitelist allowed file paths: if (in_array($file, $allowed_files)) { include $file; }

recon_summary:
- **What it does:** DVWA is a deliberately vulnerable web application for security training, demonstrating common web vulnerabilities such as SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, file inclusion, command execution, and insecure uploads.

- **Tech stack:** PHP web application with MySQL/MariaDB or SQLite, using a modular structure where each vulnerability has `low`, `medium`, `high`, and `impossible` implementations.

- **Untrusted input / attack surface:** User-controlled HTTP request data enters through the vulnerability module endpoints, including form fields, query parameters, file uploads, and API inputs used by modules such as `sqli/`, `xss_r/`, `xss_s/`, `csrf/`, `fi/`, `exec/`, `upload/`, `brute/`, `cryptography/`, and `api/`.

- **Riskiest component:** The `exec/` command execution module is the riskiest because it demonstrates OS command injection, which can lead to full server compromise if the application is exposed outside a controlled environment.

recon_summary:
- **What it does:** NodeGoat is an intentionally vulnerable Node.js web app, presented as “RetireEasy,” for hands-on learning and remediation of OWASP Top 10 risks.
- **Tech stack:** Node.js/Express, MongoDB, Swig, express-session, bcrypt-nodejs, node-esapi, marked, csurf, needle, helmet, with Grunt/Mocha/Cypress for testing.
- **Attack surface:** Untrusted input enters through HTTP routes such as `/login`, `/signup`, `/profile`, `/contributions`, `/allocations`, `/memos`, `/benefits`, and `/research`, including form fields, session data, and user-supplied stock symbols.
- **Riskiest component:** The `/research` feature, which makes server-side external HTTP calls via `needle` based on user input, creating a high-impact SSRF risk and reliance on an outdated dependency.

title: invoice-mailer

report.verdict: 🔴 Not safe to ship: 2 critical issue(s) need fixing now.
report.plain_summary: Your system has two serious weaknesses that could let an attacker take control if left unfixed. Three issues have already been fixed, and four smaller ones need to be watched. The biggest risks are unsafe file handling, a secret key left in the code, and not properly checking the partner connection.

items.title: OS Command Injection
items.plain: If a user can control the name of the file being compressed, they could trick the system into running malicious commands on the server, potentially taking full control of it.

items.title: Insecure Deserialization (Pickle)
items.plain: If an attacker can send a specially crafted file to be processed, the system will automatically run the malicious code hidden inside it, leading to a full system compromise.
items.fix: Use a safe format like JSON: import json; return json.loads(blob)

items.title: Hard-coded Credentials
items.plain: The secret key to access the partner portal is written in plain text in the code. If anyone sees the code, they can steal this key and access sensitive data or perform actions on your behalf.

items.title: TLS Certificate Verification Disabled
items.plain: The system is not checking if it is talking to the real partner server. An attacker could intercept the communication and steal the data or inject fake information without you knowing.
items.fix: Remove `verify=False` or ensure it is only used in controlled testing environments with proper CA bundles.

items.title: Missing Timeout in HTTP Request
items.plain: If the partner server is slow or down, your application will wait forever, potentially freezing up and becoming unresponsive to other users.
items.fix: return requests.post(portal_url, files={"f": fh}, headers={"Authorization": PORTAL_TOKEN}, timeout=10)
